KEYWORDS Heroin epidemic mathematical model; stability analysis; behavioral change; optimal control AMS CLASSIFICATION 34D20; 49J15; 92D30 1
It is a white or brown powder, or a black sticky substance known as black tar heroin [1]
It is estimated that about 23% of individuals who take these substances become dependent on it
According to the World Heath Organization (WHO), roughly 450,000 people die as a result of drug use [2]
TheNationalSurvey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH) [3] estimates that the percentage of heroin users aged twelve or above was particularly high between 2002 and 2008
Among the young adults, it is similar high from 2009 to 2012
Drug users who share needles have a higher risk of the proliferation of other diseases, like human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), Hepatitis B and C [4, 5]
The experimental new vaccine for heroin addiction, developed at the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) [1], incites the generation of antibodies, which block the effects of heroin
Sev- eral types of researches suggest that drug usage and the associated harm are highest among young people aged 18 to 25 years
During last few years, several mathematical models have been developed to de- scribetheheroinepidemic[6,7]
Here we propose a heroin epidemic disease model with control variables and study it using optimal control theory
